definition: Splitting raw text into the atomic units (tokens) that a model actually consumes.
details: A tokenizer converts text into a sequence of integer token ids, usually subword units rather than whole words, so any string can be represented with a finite vocabulary. SentencePiece is a language-agnostic subword toolkit that trains segmenters directly on raw text and is used by many multilingual models, including T5 and Llama.

explainer.lead: Tokenization splits raw text into the atomic units (tokens) a model actually consumes. It matters because it determines how any string is represented within a finite vocabulary.

tiers.eli5: Like chopping text into the exact pieces a model can read, so even new words fit.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers choose a tokenizer suited to their language and domain; SentencePiece trains segmenters directly on raw text and is used by many multilingual models, including T5 and Llama. Pitfall: a tokenizer mismatched to the domain splits text inefficiently.
tiers.paperLevel: A tokenizer converts text into a sequence of integer token ids, usually subword units rather than whole words, so any string can be represented with a finite vocabulary; SentencePiece is a language-agnostic subword toolkit.

explainer.example: A multilingual model trains a SentencePiece segmenter on raw text, then uses it to turn any input string into token ids.

citation.title: SentencePiece: A simple and language independent subword tokenizer and detokenizer for Neural Text Processing
